The same applies to the minds to be abandoned by seeing the path.
As it is with those not bound by any realm, so it is with those bound to the desire realm, the form realm, and the formless realm.
Regarding the mind associated with wrong view to be abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*), how many underlying tendencies (*anuśaya*) increase?
Answer:

It refers to the false view abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodhadarśana-prahātavya*), as well as the ignorance (*avidyā*) associated with it; furthermore, it includes those factors conditioned by outflows (*sāsrava*) abandoned through the vision of cessation, as well as the pervasive latent dispositions (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*). The same applies to the factors associated with them, and to the formations dissociated from mind (*cittaviprayukta-saṃskāra*) that arise together with them, which are conditioned by outflows and abandoned through the vision of cessation, as well as the pervasive latent dispositions.
Regarding the mind associated with doubt that is to be abandoned by the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*), how many latent tendencies (*anuśaya*) increase?
Answer:
The doubt to be abandoned by the vision of cessation, as well as the ignorance (*avidyā*) associated with it.

If it is a latent disposition (anuśaya) abandoned by the vision of cessation that takes impure objects as its condition, or if it is a universal latent disposition, the same applies to the associated factors; and regarding those co-arising formations dissociated from mind, it applies to those abandoned by the vision of cessation that take impure objects as their condition and to the universal latent dispositions.
Regarding the mind associated with wrong view and doubt that is to be abandoned by the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-heya*), how many underlying tendencies (*anuśaya*) increase?
Answer:
The wrong view and doubt to be abandoned by the vision of cessation, as well as the ignorance (*avidyā*) associated with them.

If there are outflow-tainted objects to be abandoned by the vision of cessation, or if there are pervasive latent dispositions (*anuśaya*), the same applies to their associated dharmas; and regarding the non-associated formations (*cittaviprayuktasaṃskāra*) arising from them, [the same applies] to those outflow-tainted objects to be abandoned by the vision of cessation and to the pervasive latent dispositions.
Regarding the mind dissociated from the false view abandoned by the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*), how many latent tendencies (*anuśaya*) increase?
Answer:

With the exception of the false view abandoned by the vision of cessation and the ignorance (*avidyā*) associated with it, all other latent tendencies abandoned by the vision of cessation as well as the universal (*sarvatraga*) latent tendencies increase therein. It is the same for the factors associated with that mind. Furthermore, regarding the formations dissociated from mind (*citta-viprayukta-saṃskāra*) that arise simultaneously with that [mind], the latent tendencies abandoned by the vision of cessation which have outflow-objects (*sāsrava-ālambana*) and the universal latent tendencies increase.
Regarding the mind dissociated from doubt that is to be abandoned by the vision of cessation (*nirodhadarśana-prahātavya*), how many latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) increase? Answer:

With the exception of the doubt to be abandoned by the vision of cessation and the ignorance (*avidyā*) associated with it, all other latent dispositions to be abandoned by the vision of cessation as well as the universal (*sarvatraga*) latent dispositions increase therein. It is the same for the factors associated with that [mind]. Regarding the formations dissociated from mind (*cittaviprayukta-saṃskāra*) that arise along with that [mind], the latent dispositions to be abandoned by the vision of cessation which have out-flowing objects (*sāsrava-ālambana*) and the universal latent dispositions increase.
Regarding the mind that is dissociated from the false view and doubt abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*), how many latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) increase?
Answer:

With the exception of the false view and doubt abandoned through the vision of cessation, as well as the ignorance (*avidyā*) associated with them, all other latent dispositions abandoned through the vision of cessation and the universal (*sarvatraga*) latent dispositions increase therein. It is the same for the factors associated with that [mind]. Regarding the formations dissociated from mind (*citta-viprayukta-saṃskāra*) that arise simultaneously with it, the latent dispositions abandoned through the vision of cessation which have out-flowing objects (*sāsrava-ālambana*) and the universal latent dispositions increase.
The same applies to the mind abandoned by the path of seeing (*darśanamārga*).
As it is for those not bound [to a specific realm], so it is for those bound to the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*), the form realm (*rūpadhātu*), and the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu*).

Regarding the mind associated with false view (*mithyādṛṣṭi*) to be abandoned by the vision of cessation (*nirodhadarśana-prahātavya*), how many latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) increase through being an object (*ālambana*) but not through association (*saṃprayoga*); how many increase through association but not through being an object; how many increase both through being an object and through association; and how many increase neither through being an object nor through association?
Answer:

Those that increase through the object (*ālambana*) but not through association (*samprayoga*) refer to the latent tendencies (*anuśaya*) associated with outflows (*sāsrava*) that have cessation as their object, as well as the universal (*sarvatraga*) latent tendencies.
Those that increase through association but not through the object refer to the false view (*mithyādṛṣṭi*) regarding cessation and the ignorance (*avidyā*) associated with it.
Those that increase by way of being an object (*ālambana*) and also by way of association (*samprayoga*) do not exist.

Those that neither increase by way of being an object nor by way of association refer to: all other defilements abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*) that take uncontaminated objects (*anāsrava-ālambana*), excluding the false view and its associated ignorance; all non-universal (*asarvatraga*) defilements abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha*) and origin (*samudaya*); and all latent tendencies (*anuśaya*) abandoned through the vision of the path (*mārga*) and through cultivation (*bhāvanā*).

The same applies to the associated factors (*saṃprayukta-dharma*). Regarding the outflow-tainted objects (*sāsrava-ālambana*) and universal underlying tendencies (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*) that are abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-heya*), which arise together with those [factors] and are dissociated from mind (*citta-viprayukta-saṃskāra*), they increase by way of being their object (*ālambana*), not by way of association (*saṃprayoga*).
As for all other underlying tendencies, they do not increase with respect to them either by way of being their object or by way of association.

Regarding the mind associated with doubt that is to be abandoned by the vision of the cessation [of suffering], how many latent dispositions (anuśaya) increase by way of being objects of perception (ālambana) but not by way of association (saṃprayoga)? How many latent dispositions increase by way of association but not by way of being objects of perception? How many latent dispositions increase both by way of being objects of perception and by way of association? And how many latent dispositions increase neither by way of being objects of perception nor by way of association?
Answer:

Those that increase by way of the object (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*samprayoga*) are the latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) with outflow-objects (*sāsrava-ālambana*) abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*), as well as the universal (*sarvatraga*) latent dispositions.
Those that increase by way of association but not by way of the object are doubt (*vicikitsā*) abandoned through the vision of cessation and the ignorance (*avidyā*) associated with it.
Those that increase by way of being an object (*ālambana*) and also by way of association (*samprayoga*) do not exist.

Those that do not increase by way of being an object and do not increase by way of association refer to: with the exception of doubt (*vicikitsā*) abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*) and its associated ignorance (*avidyā*), all other untainted-object (*anāsrava-ālambana*) proclivities abandoned through the vision of cessation; all non-universal (*asarvatraga*) proclivities abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha*) and origin (*samudaya*); and all proclivities abandoned through the vision of the path (*mārga*) and through cultivation (*bhāvanā*).

The same applies to the associated factors (*samprayukta-dharma*). Regarding the outflow-tainted objects (*sāsrava-ālambana*) and universal latent dispositions (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*) that are to be abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-heya*), which arise together with those [factors] and are dissociated from mind (*cittaviprayukta-saṃskāra*), these increase by way of being their object (*ālambana*), not by way of association.
As for all other latent dispositions, they do not increase in relation to them because they are neither their object nor associated with them.

Regarding the mind associated with wrong view and doubt that is to be abandoned by the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-heya*), how many latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) increase by way of being objects (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*saṃprayoga*); how many increase by way of association but not by way of being objects; how many increase both by way of being objects and by way of association; and how many increase neither by way of being objects nor by way of association?
Answer:

Those that increase through the object of perception (*ālambana*) but not through association (*samprayoga*) refer to the latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) associated with outflows (*sāsrava*) and the universal (*sarvatraga*) dispositions that are abandoned by the vision of cessation (*nirodhadarśana-prahātavya*).

Those that increase through association but not through the object of perception refer to wrong view (*mithyādṛṣṭi*), doubt (*vicikitsā*), and the ignorance (*avidyā*) associated with them, all of which are abandoned by the vision of cessation.
Those that increase by way of being an object (*ālambana*) and also by way of association (*samprayoga*) do not exist.

Those that do not increase by way of being an object and do not increase by way of association refer to: with the exception of the false view, doubt, and the ignorance associated with them that are abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*), all other untainted-object (*anāsrava-ālambana*) proclivities abandoned through the vision of cessation; as well as the non-universal (*asarvatraga*) proclivities abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha*) and origin (*samudaya*); and all proclivities abandoned through the vision of the path (*mārga*) and through cultivation (*bhāvanā*).

The same applies to the associated dharmas therein. Regarding the outflow-tainted objects (*sāsrava-ālambana*) and universal latent dispositions (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*) that are to be abandoned by the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-heya*), which arise simultaneously with those [dharmas] and are dissociated from mind (*citta-viprayukta-saṃskāra*), these increase [in strength] by way of being their object (*ālambana*), but not by way of association (*saṃprayoga*).
As for all other latent dispositions, they do not increase therein either by way of being their object or by way of association.

Regarding the mind that is dissociated from wrong view abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodhadarśana-prahātavya*), how many latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) increase by way of being objects (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*samprayoga*), how many increase by way of association but not by way of being objects, how many increase both by way of being objects and by way of association, and how many increase neither by way of being objects nor by way of association?
Answer:
Those that increase by way of the object (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*samprayoga*) are the universal latent tendencies (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*).

Those that increase by way of association but not by way of the object are the remaining latent tendencies abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*) that take the untainted (*anāsrava*) as their object, excluding the false view (*mithyādṛṣṭi*) abandoned through the vision of cessation and its associated ignorance (*avidyā*).

Those that increase by way of the object (*ālambana*) and also by way of association (*samprayoga*) are the latent tendencies (*anuśaya*) with outflow (*sāsrava*) that take cessation as their object and are abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodhadarśana-prahātavya*).

Those that do not increase by way of the object nor by way of association are: the false view (*mithyādṛṣṭi*) and its associated ignorance (*avidyā*) abandoned through the vision of cessation; those non-universal (*asarvatraga*) [tendencies] abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha*) and origin (*samudaya*); and all latent tendencies abandoned through the vision of the path (*mārga*) and through cultivation (*bhāvanā*).

The same applies to the associated factors (*saṃprayukta-dharma*). Regarding the outflow-tainted objects (*sāsrava-ālambana*) and universal proclivities (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*) that are to be abandoned by the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-heya*), which arise together with those [factors] and are dissociated from the mind (*citta-viprayukta-saṃskāra*), the proclivities increase by way of being their object (*ālambana*), but not by way of association (*saṃprayoga*).
As for all other proclivities, they do not increase with respect to them because they are neither their objects nor associated with them.

Regarding the mind dissociated from doubt that is to be abandoned by the vision of the cessation [of suffering], how many latent dispositions (anuśaya) increase by way of being objects of focus (ālambana) but not by way of association (saṃprayoga)? How many increase by way of association but not by way of being objects of focus? How many increase both by way of being objects of focus and by way of association? And how many increase neither by way of being objects of focus nor by way of association?
Answer:
Those that increase by way of the object (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*samprayoga*) are the universal latent tendencies (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*).

Those that increase by way of association but not by way of the object are all other latent tendencies associated with the cessation of suffering (*nirodha-darśana-heya*) that take the untainted (*anāsrava*) as their object, excluding doubt (*vicikitsā*) abandoned through the vision of cessation and its associated ignorance (*avidyā*).

Those that increase by way of the object and also by way of association are the latent dispositions (anuśaya) with outflow-objects (*sāsrava*) to be abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*).

Those that do not increase by way of the object nor by way of association are: the doubt (*vicikitsā*) to be abandoned through the vision of cessation and its associated ignorance (*avidyā*); those non-universal (*asarvatraga*) [dispositions] to be abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha*) and origin (*samudaya*); and all latent dispositions to be abandoned through the vision of the path (*mārga*) and through cultivation (*bhāvanā*).

The same applies to the associated factors (*saṃprayukta-dharma*). Regarding the outflow-tainted objects (*sāsrava-ālambana*) and universal underlying tendencies (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*) that are abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*), which arise together with those [factors] and are dissociated from mind (*citta-viprayukta-saṃskāra*), these increase by way of being objects (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*saṃprayoga*).
As for all other underlying tendencies, they do not increase with respect to them either by way of being objects or by way of association.

Regarding the mind that is dissociated from false view and doubt abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-heya*), how many latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) increase by way of being objects (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*samprayoga*); how many increase by way of association but not by way of being objects; how many increase both by way of being objects and by way of association; and how many increase neither by way of being objects nor by way of association?
Answer:
Those that increase by way of the object (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*samprayoga*) are the universal underlying tendencies (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*).

Those that increase by way of association but not by way of the object are all other underlying tendencies associated with the cessation of suffering (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*) that take the untainted (*anāsrava*) as their object, excluding wrong view, doubt, and the ignorance associated with them.

Those that increase by way of the object (*ālambana*) and also by way of association (*samprayoga*) are the latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) with outflow (*sāsrava*) that take cessation as their object and are abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*).

Those that do not increase by way of the object nor by way of association are: the false view and doubt abandoned through the vision of cessation, along with the ignorance (*avidyā*) associated with them; those non-universal (*asarvatraga*) dispositions abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha*) and origin (*samudaya*); and all dispositions abandoned through the vision of the path (*mārga*) and through cultivation (*bhāvanā*).

The same applies to the associated factors (*saṃprayukta-dharma*). Regarding the outflow-tainted objects (*sāsrava-ālambana*) and universal proclivities (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*) that are to be abandoned by the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-heya*), which arise together with those [factors], they increase by way of being their object (*ālambana*), but not by way of association (*saṃprayoga*).
As for all other proclivities, they do not increase with respect to them either by way of being their object or by way of association.
The same applies to the mind abandoned through the path of seeing (*darśana-mārga*).
As it is for those not bound [to a specific realm], so it is for those bound to the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*), the form realm (*rūpadhātu*), and the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu*).

There are thirty-six underlying tendencies (*anuśaya*): namely, ten abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), seven abandoned through the vision of origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*), seven abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*), eight abandoned through the vision of the path (*mārga-darśana-prahātavya*), and four abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-prahātavya*).
What are the ten latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) abandoned through the vision of suffering?

They are: the view of a self-identity (*satkāyadṛṣṭi*), the view of extremes (*antagrāhadṛṣṭi*), false view (*mithyādṛṣṭi*) abandoned through the vision of suffering, the grasping at views (*dṛṣṭiparāmarśa*), the grasping at precepts and observances (*śīlavrataparāmarśa*), doubt (*vicikitsā*), attachment (*rāga*), aversion (*pratigha*), pride (*māna*), and ignorance (*avidyā*).
What are the seven underlying tendencies abandoned through the vision of the origin?
They are: wrong view, adherence to views, doubt, greed, hatred, pride, and ignorance, all of which are abandoned through the vision of the origin.
What are the seven underlying tendencies abandoned through the vision of cessation?
They are: wrong view, adherence to views, doubt, attachment, aversion, pride, and ignorance, which are abandoned through the vision of cessation.
What are the eight underlying tendencies (anuśaya) to be abandoned by the path of seeing?
They are: wrong view, adherence to views, adherence to precepts and observances, doubt, attachment, aversion, pride, and ignorance, all of which are to be abandoned by the path of seeing.
What are the four latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned through cultivation?
They are the latent dispositions of attachment, aversion, pride, and ignorance to be abandoned through cultivation.
Regarding the view of a self-identity (*satkāyadṛṣṭi*), how many latent dispositions increase in association with it?
Answer:

All latent dispositions (anuśaya) abandoned through the vision of suffering, as well as those universal [dispositions] abandoned through the vision of the origin, [are associated with their respective objects]; the same applies to the mental factors associated with them and the non-associated formations arising together with them.

As it is with the view of a self-identity, so it is with the view of extremes, the false views abandoned through the vision of suffering, the grasping at views, the grasping at precepts and observances, doubt, greed, hatred, pride, and ignorance.
Regarding the false views abandoned through the vision of the origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*), how many underlying tendencies (*anuśaya*) increase in association?
Answer:

All [underlying tendencies] abandoned through the vision of the origin, as well as the pervasive underlying tendencies (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*) abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), [increase]. This is likewise the case for their associated factors (*saṃprayukta-dharma*) and their co-arising non-associated formations (*cittaviprayukta-saṃskāra*).

As it is with wrong view abandoned through the vision of the origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*), so it is with views regarding excellence (*dṛṣṭi-parāmarśa*), doubt (*vicikitsā*), greed (*rāga*), hatred (*pratigha*), pride (*māna*), and ignorance (*avidyā*).
Regarding wrong view abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*), how many underlying tendencies (*anuśaya*) increase in association?
Answer:

It consists of the ignorance associated with the false view abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*), as well as the outflow-bound objects (*sāsrava-ālambana*) abandoned through the vision of cessation, and the universal underlying tendencies (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*).

Regarding those associated factors, it consists of the false view abandoned through the vision of cessation, the ignorance associated with it, the outflow-bound objects abandoned through the vision of cessation, and the universal underlying tendencies. Regarding the non-associated formations (*citta-viprayukta-saṃskāra*) that arise together with them, it consists of the outflow-bound objects abandoned through the vision of cessation and the universal underlying tendencies.
The same applies to doubt abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*).
Regarding the view of grasping at views (*dṛṣṭi-parāmarśa*) abandoned through the vision of cessation, how many underlying tendencies (*anuśaya*) increase?
Answer:
The latent dispositions (anuśaya) that are to be abandoned by the vision of cessation— namely,

those with outflow-objects (sāsrava-ālambana) and the universal ones (sarvatraga)— are likewise [abandoned] in relation to their associated dharmas and their co-arisen non-associated formations (citta-viprayukta-saṃskāra).
The same applies to attachment, aversion, and pride abandoned through the vision of cessation.
Regarding ignorance abandoned through the vision of cessation, how many underlying tendencies (anuśaya) increase?
Answer:

Excluding the ignorance that takes the untainted as its object and is abandoned by the vision of cessation (*nirodhadarśana-prahātavya*), there are all other latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) abandoned by the vision of cessation, as well as the universal (*sarvatraga*) latent dispositions.

Regarding their associated factors (*samprayukta-dharma*), there are all latent dispositions abandoned by the vision of cessation and the universal latent dispositions. Regarding the formations dissociated from mind (*cittaviprayukta-saṃskāra*) that arise simultaneously with them, there are the tainted objects (*sāsrava-ālambana*) abandoned by the vision of cessation and the universal latent dispositions.
The same applies to those abandoned by the path of seeing.
Regarding greed abandoned by the path of cultivation, how many underlying tendencies (anuśaya) increase in association with it?
Answer:

All latent dispositions (anuśaya) to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*), as well as the universal (*sarvatraga*) ones, are likewise [associated] with their corresponding factors and their co-arising non-associated formations (*citta-viprayukta-saṃskāra*).
The same applies to anger (*pratigha*), pride (*māna*), and ignorance (*avidyā*) abandoned by cultivation.

Regarding the view of a self-identity (*satkāyadṛṣṭi*), how many latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) increase by way of being its object (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*samprayoga*); how many increase by way of association but not by way of being its object; how many increase by way of both being its object and association; and how many increase neither by way of being its object nor by way of association?
Answer:

Those that increase through the object of perception (*ālambana*) but not through association (*samprayoga*) refer to all other [defilements] abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), as well as the universal latent tendencies (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*) abandoned through the vision of the origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*), excluding the ignorance associated with the view of a self-identity (*satkāya-dṛṣṭi-samprayukta-avidyā*).
That which increases through association but not through being an object does not exist.
That which increases both through being an object and through association refers to the ignorance associated with the view of a self-identity (*satkāyadṛṣṭi*).

Those that increase neither by way of the object nor by way of association refer to all latent dispositions (anuśaya) that are not universal and are abandoned through the vision of the origin of suffering, as well as all those abandoned through the vision of cessation, the vision of the path, and through cultivation.

Regarding those associated dharmas, those that increase by way of the object (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*samprayoga*) are: all other [defilements] to be abandoned by the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), with the exception of the view of a self-identity (*satkāyadṛṣṭi*) and its associated ignorance (*avidyā*), as well as the universal latent tendencies (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*) to be abandoned by the vision of origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*).
Regarding those that increase by way of association but not by way of being an object: there are none.
Regarding those that increase both by way of being an object and by way of association: these are the view of a self-identity (*satkāyadṛṣṭi*) and the ignorance associated with it.

Those that increase neither by way of the object nor by way of association refer to all latent dispositions (anuśaya) that are abandoned through the vision of the origin, excluding those that are universal, as well as all those abandoned through the vision of cessation, the vision of the path, and through cultivation.

Regarding those [factors], all the latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*) and the universal latent dispositions abandoned through the vision of the origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*) increase by way of being objects (*ālambana*), but not by way of association (*saṃprayoga*);
as for all other latent dispositions, they do not increase therein either by way of being objects or by way of association.

As it is with the view of a self-identity, so it is with the view of extremes, the false views abandoned through the vision of suffering, the grasping at views, the grasping at precepts and observances, doubt, greed, hatred, and pride.

Regarding the ignorance (*avidyā*) to be abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), how many latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) increase by way of being an object (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*saṃprayoga*), how many increase by way of association but not by way of being an object, how many increase both by way of being an object and by way of association, and how many do not increase either by way of being an object or by way of association?
Answer:

Those that increase by way of the object (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*samprayoga*) are the ignorance (*avidyā*) to be abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), as well as the pervasive latent tendencies (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*) to be abandoned through the vision of the origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*).
Those that increase by way of association but not by way of being an object: none exist.

Those that increase both by way of being an object and by way of association: these refer to all other latent dispositions (anuśaya) abandoned through the vision of suffering, with the exception of the ignorance abandoned through the vision of suffering.

Those that increase neither by way of the object nor by way of association refer to all latent dispositions (anuśaya) that are abandoned through the vision of the origin of suffering which are not universal, as well as those abandoned through the vision of cessation, the vision of the path, and through cultivation.

Regarding those associated dharmas, those that increase by way of the object (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*samprayoga*) are the universal latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned through the vision of the origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*).
Those that increase by way of association but not by way of the object do not exist.

Those that increase by way of the object (*ālambana*) and also by way of association (*samprayoga*) are all the latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*).

Those that do not increase by way of the object nor by way of association are the non-universal (*asarvatraga*) latent dispositions abandoned through the vision of origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*), as well as all latent dispositions abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha*), the path (*mārga*), and cultivation (*bhāvanā*).

Regarding those [factors] that arise with them, all the latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*) and the universal latent dispositions abandoned through the vision of the origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*) increase by way of being objects of perception (*ālambana*), but not by way of association (*saṃprayoga*);
as for all other latent dispositions, they do not increase therein either by way of being objects of perception or by way of association.

Regarding the false view abandoned through the vision of the origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*), how many underlying tendencies (*anuśaya*) increase by way of being objects (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*saṃprayoga*); how many increase by way of association but not by way of being objects; how many increase both by way of being objects and by way of association; and how many increase neither by way of being objects nor by way of association?
Answer:

Those that increase by way of the object (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*samprayoga*) refer to all other latent tendencies (*anuśaya*) abandoned through the vision of the origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*), as well as those abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*) that are universal (*sarvatraga*), excluding the ignorance associated with the false view abandoned through the vision of the origin.
There is no [defilement] that increases through association but not through being an object-condition (*ālambana*).

That which increases both through being an object-condition and through association refers to the ignorance associated with the false view abandoned by the vision of the origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*).

Those that increase neither by way of the object nor by way of association refer to all latent dispositions (anuśaya) that are non-universal and are to be abandoned through the vision of suffering, as well as all those to be abandoned through the vision of cessation, the vision of the path, and through cultivation.

Regarding those associated dharmas, those that increase by way of the object (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*samprayoga*) are: all other [defilements] abandoned through the vision of the origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*), with the exception of the false view (*mithyā-dṛṣṭi*) and its associated ignorance (*avidyā*) abandoned through the vision of the origin; as well as all universal latent tendencies (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*) abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*).
Regarding those that increase by way of association but not by way of being an object: there are none.

Regarding those that increase both by way of being an object and by way of association: these refer to the false view abandoned through the vision of the origin [of suffering] and the ignorance associated with it.

Those that increase neither by way of the object (*ālambana*) nor by way of association (*samprayoga*) refer to all latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) that are not universal (*asarvatraga*) and are abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), as well as those abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*), the vision of the path (*mārga-darśana-prahātavya*), and through cultivation (*bhāvanā-prahātavya*).

Regarding those [factors] that arise as mental formations dissociated from mind (*citta-viprayukta-saṃskāra*), all latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) abandoned through the vision of the origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*) and all pervasive latent dispositions (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*) abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*) increase by way of being their objects (*ālambana*), but not by way of association (*saṃprayoga*);
as for all other latent dispositions, they do not increase with respect to them either by way of being objects or by way of association.

As it is with the false view abandoned through the vision of the origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*), so it is with the grasping at views (*dṛṣṭi-parāmarśa*), doubt (*vicikitsā*), greed (*rāga*), hatred (*dveṣa*), and pride (*māna*).

Regarding the ignorance (*avidyā*) abandoned through the vision of the origin, how many latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) increase by way of being its object (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*saṃprayoga*); how many increase by way of association but not by way of being its object; how many increase both by way of being its object and by way of association; and how many increase neither by way of being its object nor by way of association?
Answer:

Those that increase by way of the object of focus (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*samprayoga*) refer to the ignorance (*avidyā*) abandoned through the vision of the origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*), as well as the pervasive latent tendencies (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*) abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*).
Those that increase by way of association but not by way of being an object do not exist.

Those that increase both by way of being an object and by way of association are all other latent dispositions (anuśaya) abandoned through the vision of the origin of suffering, with the exception of the ignorance abandoned through the vision of the origin of suffering.

Those that increase neither by way of the object nor by way of association refer to the non-universal latent dispositions abandoned through the vision of suffering, as well as all latent dispositions abandoned through the vision of cessation, the vision of the path, and through cultivation.

Regarding those associated dharmas, those that increase by way of being an object (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*samprayoga*) are the universal latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*).
Those that increase by way of association but not by way of being an object do not exist.

Those that increase by way of the object (*ālambana*) and also by way of association (*samprayoga*) are all the latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) abandoned through the vision of the origin (*samudaya-darśana-prahātavya*).

Those that do not increase by way of the object nor by way of association are the non-universal [dispositions] abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha-darśana-prahātavya*), as well as all the latent dispositions abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*), the vision of the path (*mārga-darśana-prahātavya*), and those abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-prahātavya*).

Regarding those [factors] that arise as formations dissociated from mind (*cittaviprayuktasaṃskāra*), all latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) abandoned through the vision of origin (*samudayadarśana-prahātavya*) and all pervasive latent dispositions (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*) abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkhadarśana-prahātavya*) increase by way of being their objects (*ālambanataḥ*), but not by way of association (*saṃprayogataḥ*).
As for all other latent dispositions, they do not increase with respect to them either by way of being objects or by way of association.

Regarding the false view to be abandoned by the vision of cessation (*nirodhadarśana-prahātavya*), how many latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) increase by way of being objects (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*samprayoga*), how many increase by way of association but not by way of being objects, how many increase both by way of being objects and by way of association, and how many do not increase either by way of being objects or by way of association?
Answer:

Those that increase by way of the object (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*saṃprayoga*) are the outflows-objects (*sāsrava-ālambana*) abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*), as well as the pervasive latent tendencies (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*).
Those that increase by way of association but not by way of the object are the ignorance (*avidyā*) associated with the false view (*mithyādṛṣṭi*) abandoned through the vision of cessation.
Those that increase by way of being an object (*ālambana*) and also by way of association (*samprayoga*) do not exist.

Those that do not increase by way of being an object and do not increase by way of association are: with the exception of the ignorance associated with the false view abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*), all other untainted-object (*anāsrava-ālambana*) proclivities abandoned through the vision of cessation; as well as all non-universal (*asarvatraga*) proclivities abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha*) and origin (*samudaya*); and all proclivities abandoned through the path of vision (*darśana-mārga*) and cultivation (*bhāvanā-mārga*).

Regarding those associated dharmas, those that increase by way of the object (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*samprayoga*) are the outflowing (*sāsrava*) objects and the universal (*sarvatraga*) latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodhadarśana-prahātavya*).
Those that increase through association but not through being an object are the false views to be abandoned by the vision of cessation and the ignorance associated with them.
Those that increase both through being an object and through association do not exist.

Those that increase neither by way of the object (*ālambana*) nor by way of association (*samprayoga*) refer to: with the exception of the false view (*mithyādṛṣṭi*) abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodhadarśana-prahātavya*) and its associated ignorance (*avidyā*), all other latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) abandoned through the vision of cessation that take uncontaminated objects (*anāsrava-ālambana*), as well as those abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha*) and origin (*samudaya*) that are not universal (*asarvatraga*), and all [latent dispositions] abandoned through the vision of the path (*mārga*) and through cultivation (*bhāvanā*).

Regarding those [factors] associated with the arising of mind, the outflow-tainted (*sāsrava*) objects and universal (*sarvatraga*) latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned through the vision of cessation increase by way of being their object (*ālambana*), but not by way of association (*samprayoga*);
as for all other latent dispositions, they do not increase therein either by way of being an object or by way of association.
The same applies to doubt abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*).

Regarding the view of grasping at views (*dṛṣṭi-parāmarśa*) abandoned through the vision of cessation, how many latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) increase by way of being an object (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*saṃprayoga*), how many increase by way of association but not by way of being an object, how many increase both by way of being an object and by way of association, and how many increase neither by way of being an object nor by way of association?
Answer:

Those that increase by way of the object (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*samprayoga*) refer to all other outflow-tainted objects (*sāsrava-ālambana*) abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*), as well as the universal underlying tendencies (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*), with the exception of the ignorance (*avidyā*) associated with the view of grasping at views (*dṛṣṭi-parāmarśa*) abandoned through the vision of cessation.
Regarding those that increase through association but not through being an object: there are none.

Regarding those that increase both through being an object and through association: this refers to the ignorance associated with the view of grasping at views (*dṛṣṭiparāmarśa*), which is to be abandoned by the vision of cessation (*nirodhadarśana-prahātavya*).

Those that increase neither by way of the object nor by way of association refer to the latent dispositions (anuśaya) abandoned through the vision of cessation that take the untainted as their object, those abandoned through the vision of suffering and origin that are not universal, and all those abandoned through the vision of the path and through cultivation.

Regarding those associated dharmas, those that increase by way of the object (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*samprayoga*) are: with the exception of the view of grasping at views (*dṛṣṭiparāmarśa*) abandoned through the vision of cessation and its associated ignorance (*avidyā*), all other outflow-tainted objects (*sāsravālambana*) and universal (*sarvatraga*) latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) abandoned through the vision of cessation.
Regarding those that increase by way of association but not by way of being an object: none exist.

Regarding those that increase both by way of being an object and by way of association: these refer to the view of grasping at views (*dṛṣṭiparāmarśa*) abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodhadarśana-prahātavya*), as well as the ignorance (*avidyā*) associated with it.

Those that increase neither by way of the object nor by way of association refer to: the latent tendencies (anuśaya) associated with the uncontaminated objects abandoned through the vision of cessation; those non-universal [tendencies] abandoned through the vision of suffering and origin; and all [tendencies] abandoned through the vision of the path and through cultivation.

Regarding those [factors] consisting of formations dissociated from mind that arise therein, the outflow-tainted objects and universal latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) are augmented by them through the object-condition (*ālambana*), but not through association (*samprayoga*);
as for all other latent dispositions, they are neither augmented by them through the object-condition nor through association.
The same applies to greed, hatred, and pride that are abandoned through the vision of cessation.
*Sarvāstivāda-vibhāṣā-śāstra*, Volume Four;
*Abhidharma-prakaraṇa-pāda-śāstra*, Volume Five.
Composed by the Venerable Vasumitra; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang by Imperial Decree.

The Remainder of the Fifth Chapter, “Discrimination of the Latent Dispositions” (Anuśaya-nirdeśa). Regarding the ignorance (*avidyā*) to be abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*): how many latent dispositions increase by way of being objects (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*saṃprayoga*)? How many latent dispositions increase by way of association but not by way of being objects? How many latent dispositions increase both by way of being objects and by way of association? And how many latent dispositions neither increase by way of being objects nor by way of association?
Answer:

Those that increase by way of the object (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*samprayoga*) refer to the ignorance (*avidyā*) associated with outflows (*sāsrava*) that takes cessation as its object, as well as the universal proclivities (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*).

Those that increase by way of association but not by way of the object refer to all other proclivities associated with the view of cessation that take the outflow-free (*anāsrava*) as their object, excluding the ignorance associated with the view of cessation that takes the outflow-free as its object.

Those that increase both by way of the object and by way of association refer to all other latent dispositions (anuśaya) associated with outflows (*sāsrava*) and having the cessation of suffering as their object (*nirodhālambana*), which are abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodhadarśana-prahātavya*), excluding the ignorance (*avidyā*) associated with outflows that has the cessation of suffering as its object.

Those that increase neither by way of being an object (*ālambana*) nor by way of association (*samprayoga*) refer to: the ignorance (*avidyā*) associated with the outflow-free (*anāsrava*) objects abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*); the non-universal (*asarvatraga*) proclivities abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha*) and origin (*samudaya*); and all proclivities abandoned through the vision of the path (*mārga*) and through cultivation (*bhāvanā*).
Regarding those associated dharmas, those that increase by way of the object (ālambana) but not by way of association (saṃprayoga) are the universal latent dispositions (sarvatraga-anuśaya).

Those that increase by way of association but not by way of the object are the latent dispositions associated with the cessation of suffering (nirodha-darśana-prahātavya) that have the untainted (anāsrava) as their object.

Those that increase by way of both the object (*ālambana*) and association (*samprayoga*) are the latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) with outflow (*sāsrava*) that take cessation as their object and are abandoned through the vision of cessation.

Those that do not increase by way of the object nor by way of association are the non-universal [dispositions] abandoned through the vision of suffering and origin, as well as all those abandoned through the vision of the path and through cultivation.

Regarding those formations dissociated from mind (*cittaviprayuktasaṃskāra*) that arise therein, the outflow-tainted objects (*sāsravālambana*) and universal latent dispositions (*sarvatragānuśaya*) to be abandoned by the vision of cessation increase [in strength] by way of the object (*ālambanataḥ*), but not by way of association (*saṃprayogataḥ*);
as for all other latent dispositions, they do not increase therein either by way of the object or by way of association.
The same applies to those [defilements] abandoned through the path of seeing (*darśana-mārga*).

Regarding greed abandoned through the path of cultivation (*bhāvanā-mārga*), how many latent tendencies (*anuśaya*) increase by way of being an object (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*samprayoga*), how many increase by way of association but not by way of being an object, how many increase by way of both being an object and association, and how many increase neither by way of being an object nor by way of association?
Answer:

Those that increase by way of the object (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*samprayoga*) refer to all other latent tendencies (*anuśaya*) abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*), as well as the universal (*sarvatraga*) latent tendencies, with the exception of the ignorance associated with craving abandoned through cultivation.
That which increases by way of association but not by way of being an object does not exist.
That which increases both by way of being an object and by way of association refers to the ignorance associated with greed that is abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).

Those that increase neither by way of the object nor by way of association refer to the non-universal proclivities abandoned through the vision of suffering and origin, as well as all proclivities abandoned through the vision of cessation and the path.

Regarding those associated dharmas, those that increase by way of the object (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*samprayoga*) are: with the exception of the greed abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*) and its associated ignorance (*avidyā*), all other defilements abandoned through cultivation and all pervasive (*sarvatraga*) latent tendencies (*anuśaya*).
There are none that increase by way of association but not by way of being an object.
Those that increase both by way of being an object and by way of association are the greed abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*) and the ignorance (*avidyā*) associated with it.

Those that increase neither by way of the object nor by way of association refer to the non-universal proclivities abandoned through the vision of suffering and origin, as well as all proclivities abandoned through the vision of cessation and the path.

Regarding those [factors] that arise as formations dissociated from mind (*cittaviprayuktasaṃskāra*), all latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*) and the universal latent dispositions increase by way of being their objects (*ālambana*),
but not by way of association (*samprayoga*);
as for all other latent dispositions, they do not increase by way of being their objects nor by way of association.
The same applies to hatred and pride abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).
Regarding ignorance abandoned through cultivation:

how many underlying tendencies (*anuśaya*) increase by way of being objects (*ālambana*), but not by way of association (*samprayoga*); how many increase by way of association, but not by way of being objects; how many increase both by way of being objects and by way of association; and how many increase neither by way of being objects nor by way of association?
Answer:

Those that increase by way of the object of cognition (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*samprayoga*) are the ignorance (*avidyā*) to be abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*) and the universal latent dispositions (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*).
Those that increase by way of association but not by way of the object of cognition do not exist.

Those that increase through the object (*ālambana*) and also through association (*samprayoga*) are all other latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*), with the exception of ignorance (*avidyā*) abandoned by cultivation.

Those that neither increase through the object nor through association are the non-universal (*asarvatraga*) dispositions abandoned by seeing suffering (*duḥkha-darśana*) and origin (*samudaya*), as well as all dispositions abandoned by seeing cessation (*nirodha-darśana*) and the path (*mārga-darśana*).
Regarding those associated dharmas, those that increase by way of the object (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*samprayoga*) are the universal latent dispositions (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*).
Those that increase by way of association but not by way of the object do not exist.
Those that increase by way of the object (*ālambana*) and also by way of association (*samprayoga*) are all the latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) abandoned through cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).

Those that do not increase by way of the object nor by way of association are the non-universal (*asarvatraga*) dispositions abandoned through the vision of suffering and origin (*duḥkha-samudaya-darśana-heya*), as well as all the latent dispositions abandoned through the vision of cessation and the path (*nirodha-mārga-darśana-heya*).

Regarding those formations dissociated from mind (*citta-viprayukta-saṃskāra*) that arise therein, all latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*) and the universal (*sarvatraga*) latent dispositions increase [in strength] by way of being their objects (*ālambana*), but not by way of association (*samprayoga*).
As for all other latent dispositions, they do not increase therein either by way of being objects or by way of association.

There are forty-eight types of ignorance (*avidyā*), namely: the ignorance associated with false view (*mithyādṛṣṭi*) abandoned through the vision of the cessation [of suffering]; the ignorance associated with doubt (*vicikitsā*) abandoned through the vision of the cessation; the ignorance associated with both false view and doubt abandoned through the vision of the cessation; the ignorance dissociated from false view abandoned through the vision of the cessation; the ignorance dissociated from doubt abandoned through the vision of the cessation; and the ignorance dissociated from both false view and doubt abandoned through the vision of the cessation.
The same applies to those abandoned by the path of seeing (*darśana-mārga*).
As with those not bound to any realm, so it is for those bound to the desire realm (*kāmadhātu*), the form realm (*rūpadhātu*), and the formless realm (*ārūpyadhātu*).

Regarding the ignorance (*avidyā*) associated with the false view (*mithyādṛṣṭi*) to be abandoned by the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*), how many underlying tendencies (*anuśaya*) increase?
Answer:

The false view abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodhadarśana-prahātavyā mithyādṛṣṭi*), as well as the outflow-tainted objects (*sāsravālambana*) abandoned through the vision of cessation, together with the pervasive latent tendencies (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*); regarding those associated dharmas, there is the false view abandoned through the vision of cessation and its associated ignorance (*avidyā*), whether it be the outflow-tainted objects abandoned through the vision of cessation or the pervasive latent tendencies.

Regarding those formations dissociated from mind that arise therein, there are the outflow-tainted objects (*sāsrava-ālambana*) and universal latent dispositions (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*) to be abandoned by the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*).
Regarding the ignorance associated with doubt (*vicikitsā-samprayukta-avidyā*) to be abandoned by the vision of cessation, how many latent dispositions increase (*anuśerate*)?
Answer:

Doubt abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodhadarśana-prahātavya*), along with those factors associated with it that have outflow (*sāsrava*) as their object; furthermore, the pervasive latent tendencies (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*).

Regarding the factors associated with them: doubt abandoned through the vision of cessation and the ignorance (*avidyā*) associated with it; and those factors that have outflow as their object and are abandoned through the vision of cessation, as well as the pervasive latent tendencies.

Regarding those formations dissociated from mind that arise therein, there are the outflow-tainted objects (*sāsrava-ālambana*) and the universal latent dispositions (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*) to be abandoned by the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*).
Regarding the ignorance (*avidyā*) associated with the false view and doubt to be abandoned by the vision of cessation, how many latent dispositions increase (*anuśerate*)?
Answer:

The false views and doubts abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*), as well as those with outflow directed toward [the truth of] cessation (*nirodhālambana-sāsrava*), together with the pervasive latent tendencies (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*).

Regarding their associated factors: the false views and doubts abandoned through the vision of cessation, the ignorance (*avidyā*) associated with them, those with outflow directed toward cessation, and the pervasive latent tendencies.

Regarding those formations dissociated from mind that arise therein, there are the outflow-tainted objects (*sāsrava-ālambana*) and universal latent dispositions (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*) to be abandoned by the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*).

Regarding the ignorance (*avidyā*) dissociated from the false view of cessation (*nirodha-mithyādṛṣṭi*) which is to be abandoned by the vision of cessation, how many latent dispositions increase (*anuśerate*)?
Answer:

Regarding the doubt to be abandoned by the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*), as well as the outflow-tainted objects (*sāsrava-ālambana*) to be abandoned by the vision of cessation, and the pervasive latent dispositions (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*):

with respect to the associated factors (*saṃprayukta-dharma*), excluding the false view (*mithyādṛṣṭi*) to be abandoned by the vision of cessation and the ignorance (*avidyā*) associated therewith, all other factors to be abandoned by the vision of cessation and the pervasive latent dispositions [are to be abandoned].

Regarding those formations dissociated from mind that arise therein, there are the outflow-tainted objects (*sāsrava-ālambana*) and universal latent dispositions (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*) to be abandoned by the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*).
Regarding the ignorance (*avidyā*) dissociated from doubt (*vicikitsā*) that is to be abandoned by the vision of cessation, how many latent dispositions increase (*anuśerate*)?
Answer:

The wrong view abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*), as well as the outflow-tainted objects (*sāsrava-ālambana*) abandoned through the vision of cessation, together with the pervasive latent tendencies (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*).

Regarding the factors associated with those, [the abandonments consist of] all other things abandoned through the vision of cessation and the pervasive latent tendencies, excluding the doubt abandoned through the vision of cessation and the ignorance associated with it.

Regarding those formations dissociated from mind that arise therein, there are the outflow-tainted objects (*sāsrava-ālambana*) and universal latent dispositions (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*) to be abandoned by the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*).

Regarding the ignorance (*avidyā*) dissociated from false view (*mithyādṛṣṭi*) and doubt (*vicikitsā*) which are to be abandoned by the vision of cessation, how many latent dispositions increase (*anuśerate*)?
Answer:
The outflow-tainted objects (sāsrava-ālambana) abandoned through the vision of cessation, as well as the pervasive latent tendencies (sarvatraga-anuśaya).

Regarding their associated dharmas, this includes all other factors abandoned through the vision of cessation and all pervasive latent tendencies, with the exception of the false view, doubt, and the ignorance associated with them that are themselves abandoned through the vision of cessation.

Regarding those [factors] that arise as mental formations dissociated from mind (*cittaviprayuktasaṃskāra*), there are the outflow-tainted objects (*sāsravālambana*) and universal underlying tendencies (*sarvatragānuśaya*) to be abandoned by the vision of cessation (*nirodhadarśana-prahātavya*);
the same applies to those to be abandoned by the vision of the path (*mārgadarśana-prahātavya*).
As it is with those not bound by any realm, so it is with those bound to the desire realm, the form realm, and the formless realm.

Regarding the ignorance associated with the false view to be abandoned by the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*), how many latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) increase by way of being objects (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*samprayoga*); how many increase by way of association but not by way of being objects; how many increase both by way of being objects and by way of association; and how many increase neither by way of being objects nor by way of association?
Answer:

Those that increase by way of the object (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*samprayoga*) are the latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) associated with outflows (*sāsrava*) that take cessation as their object, as well as the universal (*sarvatraga*) latent dispositions.
Those that increase by way of association but not by way of the object are the false views (*mithyādṛṣṭi*) abandoned through the vision of cessation.
Those that increase by way of being an object (*ālambana*) and also by way of association (*samprayoga*) do not exist.

Those that neither increase by way of being an object nor by way of association refer to all other latent tendencies (*anuśaya*) abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*) that take the untainted (*anāsrava*) as their object, excluding wrong view (*mithyādṛṣṭi*); those abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha*) and origin (*samudaya*) that are not universal (*asarvatraga*); and all [latent tendencies] abandoned through the vision of the path (*mārga*) and through cultivation (*bhāvanā*).

Regarding those associated dharmas, those that increase by way of the object (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*samprayoga*) are the outflow-tainted objects (*sāsrava-ālambana*) abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*) and the universal latent tendencies (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*).

Those that increase through association but not through being an object are the false views to be abandoned by the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*) and the ignorance associated with them.
Those that increase both through being an object and through association do not exist.

Those that increase neither by way of the object (*ālambana*) nor by way of association (*samprayoga*) refer to: with the exception of the false view (*mithyādṛṣṭi*) abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodhadarśana-prahātavya*) and its associated ignorance (*avidyā*), all other latent tendencies (*anuśaya*) abandoned through the vision of cessation that take the untainted as their object; those abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha*) and origin (*samudaya*) that are not universal (*asarvatraga*); and all latent tendencies abandoned through the vision of the path (*mārga*) and through cultivation (*bhāvanā*).

Regarding those formations dissociated from mind (*cittaviprayuktasaṃskāra*) that arise therein, the outflow-tainted objects (*sāsravālambana*) and universal latent dispositions (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*) to be abandoned by the vision of cessation increase [in strength] by way of being their object (*ālambanataḥ*), but not by way of association (*saṃprayogataḥ*);
as for all other latent dispositions, they do not increase therein either by way of being their object or by way of association.

Regarding the ignorance associated with doubt that is to be abandoned by the vision of the cessation [of suffering], how many latent dispositions (anuśaya) increase by way of being objects of perception (ālambana) but not by way of association (saṃprayoga)? How many increase by way of association but not by way of being objects of perception? How many increase both by way of being objects of perception and by way of association? And how many increase neither by way of being objects of perception nor by way of association?
Answer:

Those that increase by way of the object (ālambana) but not by way of association (saṃprayoga) are the outflows-objects (sāsrava-ālambana) and the universal proclivities (sarvatraga-anuśaya) abandoned through the vision of cessation (nirodha-darśana-prahātavya).
Those that increase by way of association but not by way of the object are the doubt (vicikitsā) abandoned through the vision of cessation.
Those that increase by way of being an object (*ālambana*) and also by way of association (*samprayoga*) do not exist.

Those that neither increase by way of being an object nor by way of association refer to: all other defilements abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*) that take the untainted (*anāsrava*) as their object, excluding doubt; all non-universal (*asarvatraga*) defilements abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha*) and origin (*samudaya*); and all latent tendencies (*anuśaya*) abandoned through the vision of the path (*mārga*) and through cultivation (*bhāvanā*).

Regarding those associated dharmas, those that increase by way of the object (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*samprayoga*) are the outflow-tainted objects (*sāsrava-ālambana*) abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*) and the universal proclivities (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*).
Those that increase by way of association but not by way of being an object are doubt abandoned through the vision of cessation and the ignorance associated with it.
Those that increase both by way of being an object and by way of association do not exist.

Those that increase neither by way of the object (*ālambana*) nor by way of association (*samprayoga*) refer to: with the exception of doubt (*vicikitsā*) abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*) and its associated ignorance (*avidyā*), all other untainted-object (*anāsrava-ālambana*) proclivities abandoned through the vision of cessation; those non-universal (*asarvatraga*) proclivities abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha*) and origin (*samudaya*); and all proclivities abandoned through the vision of the path (*mārga*) and through cultivation (*bhāvanā*).

Regarding those formations dissociated from mind (*cittaviprayuktasaṃskāra*) that arise therein, the outflow-tainted objects (*sāsravālambana*) and universal latent dispositions (*sarvatragānuśaya*) to be abandoned by the vision of cessation increase [in strength] through the object (*ālambanataḥ*), but not through association (*saṃprayogataḥ*);
as for all other latent dispositions, they do not increase therein either through the object or through association.

Regarding the ignorance associated with wrong view and doubt that is to be abandoned by the vision of cessation (*nirodhadarśana-prahātavya*), how many latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) increase by way of being objects (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*samprayoga*); how many increase by way of association but not by way of being objects; how many increase both by way of being objects and by way of association; and how many increase neither by way of being objects nor by way of association?
Answer:

Those that increase through the object (*ālambana*) but not through association (*samprayoga*) refer to the outflows-based (*sāsrava-ālambana*) and universal (*sarvatraga*) latent tendencies (*anuśaya*) to be abandoned by the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*).
Those that increase through association but not through the object refer to wrong view (*mithyādṛṣṭi*) and doubt (*vicikitsā*) to be abandoned by the vision of cessation.
Those that increase by way of being an object (*ālambana*) and also by way of association (*samprayoga*) do not exist.

Those that neither increase by way of being an object nor by way of association refer to: all other defilements abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*) that take the untainted (*anāsrava*) as their object, excluding wrong view (*mithyādṛṣṭi*) and doubt (*vicikitsā*); those abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha*) and origin (*samudaya*) that are not universal (*asarvatraga*); and all latent tendencies (*anuśaya*) abandoned through the vision of the path (*mārga*) and through cultivation (*bhāvanā*).

Regarding those associated dharmas, those that increase by way of the object (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*samprayoga*) are the outflow-tainted objects (*sāsrava-ālambana*) abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*) and the universal proclivities (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*).
Those that increase through association but not through being an object are: wrong view, doubt, and the ignorance associated with them, which are to be abandoned by the vision of cessation.
Those that increase both through being an object and through association do not exist.

Those that increase neither by way of the object (*ālambana*) nor by way of association (*samprayoga*) refer to: with the exception of the false view, doubt, and the ignorance associated with them that are to be abandoned by seeing the cessation [of suffering] (*nirodha-darśana-heya*), all other untainted-object (*anāsrava-ālambana*) proclivities to be abandoned by seeing the cessation; those non-universal (*asarvatraga*) proclivities to be abandoned by seeing the suffering and origin [of suffering]; and all proclivities to be abandoned by seeing the path (*mārga-darśana-heya*) and by cultivation (*bhāvanā-heya*).

Regarding those formations dissociated from mind that arise therein, the outflow-tainted objects (*sāsrava-ālambana*) and universal latent dispositions (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*) to be abandoned by the vision of cessation increase [in strength] by way of being their object (*ālambana*), but not by way of association (*samprayoga*);
as for all other latent dispositions, they do not increase therein either by way of being their object or by way of association.

Regarding the ignorance that is dissociated from the false view to be abandoned by the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya-mithyādṛṣṭi-viprayukta-avidyā*), how many latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) increase through being an object (*ālambana*) but not through association (*saṃprayoga*), how many increase through association but not through being an object, how many increase through both being an object and through association, and how many increase neither through being an object nor through association?
Answer:

Those that increase by way of the object (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*samprayoga*) refer to the outflows-based ignorance (*sāsravālambanāvidyā*) and the universal latent dispositions (*sarvatragānuśaya*) abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodhadarśana-prahātavya*).
Those that increase by way of association but not by way of the object refer to doubt (*vicikitsā*) abandoned through the vision of cessation.

Those that increase both by way of the object and by way of association refer to all other latent dispositions (anuśaya) abandoned through the vision of cessation that take contaminated objects, with the exception of the ignorance (avidyā) abandoned through the vision of cessation that takes contaminated objects as its object.

Those that increase neither by way of the object (*ālambana*) nor by way of association (*samprayoga*) refer to: with the exception of doubt (*vicikitsā*) abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*), all other latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) abandoned through the vision of cessation that take the untainted (*anāsrava*) as their object; those abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha*) and origin (*samudaya*) that are not universal (*asarvatraga*); and all latent dispositions abandoned through the vision of the path (*mārga*) and through cultivation (*bhāvanā*).
Regarding those associated dharmas, those that increase by way of the object (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*samprayoga*) are the universal latent dispositions (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*).

Those that increase by way of association but not by way of the object are all other latent dispositions with respect to the untainted (*anāsrava*) that are abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*), excluding the false view (*mithyādṛṣṭi*) abandoned through the vision of cessation and its associated ignorance (*avidyā*).

Those that increase by way of the object (*ālambana*) and also by way of association (*samprayoga*) are the latent tendencies (*anuśaya*) with outflow (*sāsrava*) that take [the Truth of] Cessation as their object and are abandoned through the vision of cessation.

Those that do not increase by way of the object nor by way of association are: the false view (*mithyādṛṣṭi*) abandoned through the vision of cessation and its associated ignorance (*avidyā*); those non-universal (*asarvatraga*) latent tendencies abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha*) and origin (*samudaya*); and all latent tendencies abandoned through the vision of the path (*mārga*) and through cultivation (*bhāvanā*).

Regarding those [factors], the dissociated formations (*cittaviprayuktasaṃskāra*), the outflow-tainted objects (*sāsravālambana*) abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodhadarśana-prahātavya*), and the universal underlying tendencies (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*) increase by way of being their object (*ālambana*), but not by way of association (*saṃprayoga*).
As for all other underlying tendencies, they do not increase by way of being their object, nor do they increase by way of association.

Regarding the ignorance (*avidyā*) dissociated from doubt that is to be abandoned by the vision of cessation (*nirodhadarśana-prahātavya*): how many underlying tendencies (*anuśaya*) increase through being an object (*ālambana*) but not through association (*saṃprayoga*), how many increase through association but not through being an object, how many increase through both being an object and through association, and how many increase neither through being an object nor through association?
Answer:

Those that increase by way of the object (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*samprayoga*) are the outflowing ignorance (*sāsrava-avidyā*) and the universal latent dispositions (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*) abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*).
Those that increase by way of association but not by way of the object are the false views (*mithyādṛṣṭi*) abandoned through the vision of cessation.

Those that increase both by way of the object and by way of association refer to all other latent dispositions (anuśaya) abandoned through the vision of cessation that take contaminated objects, excluding the ignorance (avidyā) abandoned through the vision of cessation that takes contaminated objects as its object.

Those that increase neither by way of the object (*ālambana*) nor by way of association (*samprayoga*) refer to: with the exception of the false view (*mithyādṛṣṭi*) abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodhadarśana-prahātavya*), all other untainted-object (*anāsravālambana*) defilements abandoned through the vision of cessation; those non-universal (*asarvatraga*) defilements abandoned through the vision of suffering (*duḥkha*) and origin (*samudaya*); and all latent tendencies (*anuśaya*) abandoned through the vision of the path (*mārga*) and through cultivation (*bhāvanā*).
Regarding those associated dharmas, those that increase by way of the object (*ālambana*) but not by way of association (*samprayoga*) are the universal latent dispositions (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*).

Those that increase by way of association but not by way of the object are the remaining latent dispositions abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*) that have the uncontaminated (*anāsrava*) as their object, excluding doubt (*vicikitsā*) abandoned through the vision of cessation and its associated ignorance (*avidyā*).

Those that increase by way of the object (*ālambana*) and also by way of association (*samprayoga*) are the latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) with outflow (*sāsrava*) that take cessation as their object and are abandoned through the vision of cessation.

Those that do not increase by way of the object nor by way of association are: the doubt abandoned through the vision of cessation and its associated ignorance; the non-universal [defilements] abandoned through the vision of suffering and origin; and all latent dispositions abandoned through the path and through cultivation.

Regarding those formations dissociated from mind (*cittaviprayuktasaṃskāra*) that arise therein, the outflow-tainted objects (*sāsravālambana*) and universal latent dispositions (*sarvatragānuśaya*) to be abandoned by the vision of cessation increase [in strength] by way of the object (*ālambanataḥ*), but not by way of association (*samprayogataḥ*);
as for all other latent dispositions, they do not increase therein either by way of the object or by way of association.

Regarding the ignorance (*avidyā*) that is dissociated from wrong view (*mithyādṛṣṭi*) and doubt (*vicikitsā*) abandoned through the vision of cessation (*nirodhadarśana-prahātavya*): how many latent dispositions (*anuśaya*) increase by way of being an object (*ālambana*), but not by way of association (*saṃprayoga*); how many increase by way of association, but not by way of being an object; how many increase both by way of being an object and by way of association; and how many increase neither by way of being an object nor by way of association?
Answer:

Those that increase through the object (*ālambana*) but not through association (*samprayoga*) refer to the outflows-based ignorance (*asravālambanā avidyā*) and the universal proclivities (*sarvatraga-anuśaya*) abandoned by the vision of cessation (*nirodha-darśana-prahātavya*).
Those that increase through association but not through the object do not exist.
